data.title: Institutional Property Advisors Brokers Sale of 599-Unit Multifamily Property in Portland, Oregon
data.description:
Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap () dedicated to serving the company’s institutional clients, announced today the sale of Wimbledon Square and Gardens, a 599-unit multifamily property in Portland, Oregon.

“Encompassing nearly 14.5 acres, Wimbledon Square and Gardens sits on one of the largest contiguous multifamily sites in Portland,” said Anthony Palladino, IPA senior director investments. “This was a generational opportunity to acquire a large, low-density asset in Southeast Portland, a submarket with no properties of 50 or more units in the supply pipeline.” Palladino, Philip Assouad, Giovanni Napoli, Ryan Harmon, and Nick Ruggiero of IPA, in association with David Tabata, Marcus & Millichap’s broker of record in Oregon, represented the seller and procured the buyer, FPA Multifamily.

“Institutional investors remain selective, with a growing emphasis on asset quality and opportunities to create value,” said Andrew Leahy, senior managing director, national division leader, IPA Multifamily. “Transactions of this scale demonstrate that well-positioned multifamily assets continue to attract meaningful institutional interest, even as investors maintain a disciplined approach to acquisitions.”

The property is adjacent to the Reed College campus and near D.A. Grout Elementary School and Cleveland High School. The nearby SE 17th Avenue and Holgate Boulevard MAX Light Rail Orange Line station provides direct access to Oregon Health & Science University, one of the region’s major employers. The surrounding neighborhoods of Sellwood, Woodstock, Division, and Hawthorne offer access to restaurants, retail shops, grocery stores, farmers markets, parks and trails. The property also offers convenient access to Downtown Portland.

Constructed in phases in 1973 and 1975, Wimbledon Square and Gardens comprises 83 three-story residential buildings offering studio, one-, and two-bedroom apartments and townhomes. Community amenities include three outdoor heated swimming pools with sundecks, a clubhouse, and tennis, basketball, and volleyball courts.

About Institutional Property Advisors (IPA)

Institutional Property Advisors (IPA) is a division of Marcus & Millichap (), a leading commercial real estate services firm in North America. IPA’s combination of real estate investment and capital markets expertise, industry-leading technology, and acclaimed research offers customized solutions for the acquisition, disposition and financing of institutional properties and portfolios. For more information, please visit www.institutionalpropertyadvisors.com

About Marcus & Millichap, Inc. ()

Marcus & Millichap, Inc. is a leading brokerage firm specializing in commercial real estate investment sales, financing, research and advisory services with offices throughout the United States and Canada. Marcus & Millichap closed 8,818 transactions with a sales volume of $50.8 billion in 2025. The company had 1,808 investment sales and financing professionals in more than 80 offices who provide investment brokerage and financing services to sellers and buyers of commercial real estate at year end. For additional information, please visit www.MarcusMillichap.com.

About FPA

FPA Multifamily, a privately held real estate investment firm with over 40 years of experience, specializes in acquiring, managing and repositioning multifamily properties across the United States. With approximately $17 billion in assets under management, FPA Multifamily has transacted on approximately $31 billion worth of assets, including 870 buildings and over 170,000 units, showcasing their expertise in identifying and capitalizing on value-add and core-plus opportunities in major US cities.

data.title: Bending Spoons to Buy Mailchimp, Raises Outlook
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Bending Spoons said it is buying Intuit's Mailchimp and raised its full-year outlook.

The Italian web-services firm agreed to buy Mailchimp, an email automation platform for business, for $3.68 billion, which includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in stock.

Alongside the deal, Bending Spoons entered a private placement with institutional investors to sell 32.5 million shares, with expected proceeds of $1.3 billion.

Bending Spoon shares rose 11% to $46.25 after the bell.

For the third quarter, Bending Spoons posted a profit of $90.2 million, or 13 cents a share, compared with $84.6 million, or 14 cents a share, a year earlier.

Adjusted earnings per share were 42 cents, compared with analyst estimates of 32 cents, according to FactSet.

Revenue more than doubled to $780.2 million, beating analyst estimates of $745.9 million.

The company, which went public in July, said sales growth was primarily driven by acquisitions. Since the third quarter of last year, it has acquired Airtable, AOL, Harvest, MilelQ, Tractive and Vimeo.

Bending Spoons revealed last month that Berkshire Hathaway built a 4% stake in the company. The Milan-based company said at the time it would use the fresh funds to pursue additional acquisitions.

For the current fourth quarter, Bending Spoons expects revenue of $984 million to $1 billion, which would be ahead of the $854.2 million that analysts project.

It raised its outlook for the full year to a revenue range of $3.07 billion to $3.09 billion, up from its previous guidance of $2.78 billion to $2.82 billion.

The higher outlook includes contributions from Airtable and the digital planning platform Miro, which it agreed to buy in September.

data.title: Guardant Health Launches Guardant Reveal® Ultra to Deliver Leading Sensitivity in MRD Testing
data.description:
Guardant Health, Inc. (), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the U.S. clinical launch of Guardant Reveal® Ultra, a new molecular residual disease (MRD) platform for solid tumors offering personalized, ultra-sensitive detection of residual cancer. Built on Guardant’s Smart Platform, Reveal Ultra incorporates tumor-informed, patient-specific genomic alterations to provide one of the most advanced and actionable views of MRD.

Validated on thousands of clinical samples, Guardant Reveal Ultra has demonstrated detection sensitivity of 1 part per million (ppm) or below across major tumor types. The test incorporates patient-specific alterations from thousands of genomic targets spanning all major variant classes, including structural variants. Guardant Reveal Ultra has also been validated with tissue samples containing as little as 5% tumor cellularity, significantly below the typical industry requirement of 20%, enabling testing across a broader range of clinical specimens.

“Reveal Ultra opens a new frontier in MRD detection,” said Helmy Eltoukhy, Guardant Health chairman and co-CEO. “While detecting cancer at one part per million has become an important benchmark, what truly matters is delivering that level of sensitivity reliably across real clinical samples and a broad range of tumor types. Reveal Ultra was built to meet that challenge, bringing extraordinary precision to everyday clinical practice and advancing our ability to track and manage each patient’s cancer throughout their journey.”

Guardant Reveal Ultra is designed as a connected experience, enabling physicians the option of a direct path from MRD detection to clinical action through Guardant360® Liquid. Together with Guardant Reveal®’s best-in-class tissue-free MRD detection and therapy monitoring capabilities, and Guardant360 Liquid and Guardant360® Tissue for comprehensive genomic profiling, Guardant Reveal Ultra completes Guardant’s precision oncology portfolio. These solutions work hand-in-hand to support physicians in selecting therapies, monitoring treatment response, detecting residual disease, and managing cancer throughout the patient journey.

About Guardant Health

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. For more information, visit guardanthealth.com and follow the company on LinkedIn, X (Twitter) and Facebook.

data.title: Intuit to Sell Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Intuit agreed to sell its email automation platform Mailchimp for $3.68 billion.

The fintech, which offers tax and accounting services, said it would sell the platform to Bending Spoons for $3.31 billion of cash and $368 million of Bending Spoons stock.

Intuit also posted higher profit and revenue in the fiscal first quarter.

Profit rose to $695 million, or $2.59 a share, compared with $446 million, or $1.59 a share, a year earlier.

Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted per-share earnings were $2.91, ahead of the $2.46 anticipated by analysts, according to FactSet.

Revenue rose 12% to $4.35 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $4.30 billion. Sales in Intuit's business-facing segment increased 15%, while its consumer-facing sales rose 7%.

Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million in the quarter. Intuit said selling the business will allow the company to sharpen its focus on helping clients win new customers and manage their pipeline.

The sale of the business is expected to close early in 2027. Intuit plans to use cash proceeds to buy back shares of its stock within fiscal 2027.

Intuit now expects full-year revenue to be $23.08 billion to $23.37 billion, compared with its earlier range of $23.28 billion to $23.51 billion. It expects earnings per share of $20.12 to $20.36.

data.title: US stocks slump as Anthropic soars in debut
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes slide; Nasdaq ends off most, down 2.25%
  • All S&P 500 sectors red; consumer discretionary weakest group
  • VIX hits highest intraday level since March 31
  • Dollar, US crude rise; bitcoin down >1%; gold down >2%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield dips to ~5.05%

US STOCKS SLUMP AS ANTHROPIC SOARS IN DEBUT

After a strong start to the trading day, stocks reversed course and closed sharply lower, with each of the major indexes closing down more than 2%, as the enthusiasm about the debut for Anthropic shares failed to dampen concerns about challenges facing the broader market.

After pricing at $83 per share, Anthropic opened at $111.50 before eventually closing up 17.1% at $97.17, in another test of investor appetite for AI-related stocks.

Each of the 11 major S&P 500 CBOE:SPX sectors closed in the red, with consumer discretionary the worst-performing group as Williams-Sonoma plunged 15.2% after its quarterly results and outlook.

Among the few bright spots, Palo Alto Networks closed up 6.4% after the cybersecurity firm raised its annual revenue forecast and agreed to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, which helped other stocks in the sector rally in a session that saw fewer than 40 S&P 500 components end in positive territory.

The selloff helped push Treasury yields lower in a safe-haven bid, even as Federal Reserve officials continue to express concerns about inflation and the need for more rate hikes from the central bank.

The decline marked the sixth straight for the S&P 500, its longest since April 2024, and the index is now down more than 5% on the week, putting it on pace for its biggest weekly percentage decline since the week ended April 4, 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his sweeping global tariffs.

"There are so many forces acting on the market right now that Anthropic's not going to carry the overall market by itself — you have uncertainty around Nvidia, you have Palo Alto Networks last night, " said Ellen Hazen, chief market strategist at F.L. Putnam Investment Management in Lynnfield, Massachusetts. "You have people increasingly concerned about some of the cyberattacks that we've seen in recent days. You have Xi, Putin, Trump. There's a lot of stuff going on."

data.title: Goodwin Procter fights ex-associate's subpoena demand in US insider trading case
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

Goodwin Procter is urging a federal judge to reject a subpoena for documents by a former associate who is charged with stealing information from the law firm to fuel an insider trading scheme.

The firm in a brief filed in federal court in Boston on Wednesday said that Nicolo Nourafchan is improperly seeking an order that would force it to turn over records on the same attorney-client privileged information that he is accused of stealing in the first place.

Goodwin, which is identified in court papers as simply "Law Firm C," said it had cooperated with the investigation into the scheme and that Nourafchan already had relevant, non-privileged documents it and other law firms had turned over to prosecutors.

Yet Nourafchan is now asking US Magistrate Judge Judith Dein to approve a subpoena seeking documents concerning the deals at issue along with access logs and internal communications, a demand that Goodwin's attorneys say is over broad and premature, as the criminal case against him may resolve without a trial.

"Now he asks the Court to order his alleged victims to reopen — at their own expense — their private files for a civil-style fishing expedition," wrote Goodwin's attorneys, led by Zachary Hafer of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett.

Martin Weinberg, Nourafchan's attorney, in a statement said he looked forward to arguing in favor of the subpoena at a hearing on Monday.

He argued his client is "entitled to subpoena law firm documents exculpatory to the defendant, in part because the law firm has produced documents when requested by the Government despite its current claims of privilege."

Thirty-one people overall have been charged over what prosecutors say was a decade-long scheme in which attorneys used confidential ​information from their law firms to tip off an insider trading ring about nearly 30 underway mergers.

Prosecutors said Nourafchan, while working at Sidley Austin, Latham & Watkins and Goodwin, beginning in 2014, tipped off personal injury attorney Robert Yadgarov and others to impending corporate transactions in exchange for kickbacks generated from any trading profits.

Nourafchan and ‌Yadgarov ⁠also recruited other attorneys into the scheme to feed tips to them, including one who worked at Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz and another who was employed by Weil, Gotshal & Manges and Willkie Farr & Gallagher.

In seeking to subpoena Sidley, Latham and Goodwin, Weinberg argued that Nourafchan in mounting a defense was entitled to documents in their possession that "bear directly on whether Mr. Nourafchan obtained and misused material nonpublic information as alleged."

All three law firms are considered victims by prosecutors. Sidley Austin and Latham in filings this week said they are working with Weinberg to reach agreements on the appropriate scope of subpoenas.

Both Nourafchan and Yadgarov have pleaded not guilty to securities fraud and other charges. No trial date has been set.

The case is United States v. Fejal, US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, No. 1:26-cr-10133.

For the United States: Kaitlin O'Donnell of the US Attorney's Office for the District of Massachusetts

For Nourafchan: Martin Weinberg

For Goodwin Procter: Zachary Hafer of Simpson Thacher & Bartlett

For Sidley Austin: Jack Pirozzolo of Sidley Austin
